definition_zh: 表达；表情；词语；表达式
definition_en: the act of showing thoughts or feelings; a look on the face; a word or phrase; a group of symbols in mathematics
core_image: 一张脸上清晰写出的喜怒，以及说出口的一句话
scene: 她的脸上露出惊讶的表情。A look of surprise appeared in her expression.
sceneCN: 这里 expression 是「表情」（第 2 个义项）；句意：她的脸上露出惊讶的表情。

senses.title: Showing feelings
senses.definition: the act of showing thoughts or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 表现思想或感情的行为
senses.example: Music gives her a way of expression.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐给了她一种表达方式。
senses.why: The core sense is pressing something out into view.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是把内心的东西压出来让人看见。

senses.title: A look on the face
senses.definition: a look that shows what someone feels
senses.definitionCN: 显示某人感受的面部神情
senses.example: His expression softened when he saw the child.
senses.exampleCN: 看到孩子时，他的表情柔和下来。
senses.why: Inner feeling becomes visible on the face.
senses.whyCN: 内心的感受在脸上变得可见。

senses.title: A word or phrase
senses.definition: a word or group of words used in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式使用的词或词组
senses.example: That expression is common in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 那种说法在北方很常见。
senses.why: A way of speaking becomes a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 一种说话方式变成固定的词语。

senses.title: Mathematical symbols
senses.definition: a group of symbols that shows a mathematical idea
senses.definitionCN: 表示数学概念的一组符号
senses.example: The student simplified the expression.
senses.exampleCN: 学生化简了这个表达式。
senses.why: A clear statement of meaning becomes a symbol group.
senses.whyCN: 清楚表达含义变成一组符号。

intro.en: Expression comes from Latin expressio, from exprimere, to press out.
intro.cn: expression 来自拉丁语 expressio，根源是 exprimere（压出来）。

items.en: Exprimere means to press out.
items.cn: exprimere 意为压出来。

items.en: Expressio means a pressing out.
items.cn: expressio 意为压出。

items.en: Expression keeps the sense of making clear.
items.cn: 古法语中 expression 保留「使清楚」之义。

items.en: Expression names both the act and the look.
items.cn: expression 同时指表达行为与神情。

items.en: Expression also names phrases and formulas.
items.cn: 现代英语中 expression 也指词语与公式。

note.en: Expression is what comes out; impression is what goes in.
note.cn: expression 是表达出来的东西，impression 则是留在心里的印象。

entries.definition: an idea or feeling left in the mind
the act of becoming larger
a detailed explanation
a small group of words
an expression on the face
the words used to say something

normalIntro.en: Expression is the noun of express, covering feelings, faces, phrases, and formulas.
normalIntro.cn: expression 是 express 的名词，涵盖情感、表情、词语与公式。

normal.en: Her expression showed that she was tired.
normal.cn: 她的表情说明她累了。

normal.en: Freedom of expression is protected by law.
normal.cn: 表达自由受法律保护。

normal.en: He used a polite expression to refuse.
normal.cn: 他用礼貌的说法拒绝了。

normal.en: The teacher explained the mathematical expression.
normal.cn: 老师讲解了这个数学表达式。

normal.en: Dance is a powerful form of expression.
normal.cn: 舞蹈是一种有力的表达形式。

abstract.en: Picture a face that says everything without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张不用说话就能说明一切的脸。

abstract.en: Imagine a phrase repeated by a whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被整个小镇反复使用。

abstract.en: Think of symbols lined up like a short sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象符号排成一列，像一句简短的话。

examples.en: Her expression changed when she heard the name.
examples.cn: 听到那个名字时，她的表情变了。

examples.en: The essay is full of vivid expressions.
examples.cn: 这篇文章充满生动的表达。

examples.en: Simplify the expression before solving it.
examples.cn: 解之前先化简这个表达式。

dict_mnemonic.text: express 加名词后缀 -ion，表示「表达出来的东西」，就是 expression。

root: 源自拉丁语 expressio（压出），由 exprimere 派生，核心义「把内在之物表达出来」及其结果。

sensesIntro.en: Expression means the act of showing feeling, a facial look, a phrase, or a mathematical formula.
sensesIntro.cn: expression 意为表达行为、面部表情、词语说法，或数学表达式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feeling pressed out onto a face or into words.
core.cn: 核心意象：情感被压出到脸上或话语里。

branches.en: The base sense is the act of showing feeling.
branches.cn: 基础义是表现感情的行为。

branches.en: Feeling becomes visible on the face.
branches.cn: 感受在脸上变得可见。

branches.en: A way of speaking becomes a fixed phrase.
branches.cn: 说话方式变成固定词语。

branches.en: Clear meaning becomes a group of symbols.
branches.cn: 清楚的含义变成一组符号。

branches.en: Inner expression and facial expression are closely linked.
branches.cn: 内在表达与面部表情紧密相连。

intro.en: Expression is express plus -ion, a common Latin noun ending.
intro.cn: expression 由 express 加 -ion 构成，-ion 是常见的拉丁名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin expressio and exprimere are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expressio 与 exprimere 是来源形式。

items.meaning: the act or result of expressing
items.example: Her expression was calm.
items.exampleCN: 她的表情很平静。

items.example: The book explains common expressions.
items.exampleCN: 这本书讲解常用表达。

items.example: He expressed his thanks.
items.exampleCN: 他表达了感谢。

items.example: The music is deeply expressive.
items.exampleCN: 这段音乐极富表现力。

items.example: He watched with an expressionless face.
items.exampleCN: 他面无表情地看着。

items.example: She sang expressively.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力地演唱。

items.example: The rule expressly forbids it.
items.exampleCN: 规定明确禁止这样做。

items.example: -Ion forms expression.
items.exampleCN: -ion 构成 expression。

items.meaning: a feeling left in the mind
items.example: The city made a strong impression.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市给人留下深刻印象。

definition_zh: 富于表现力的；表情丰富的；意味深长的
definition_en: showing feelings or meaning clearly and strongly
core_image: 一张脸或一段旋律把情绪推到观看者眼前，遮都遮不住
scene: 朗读课上，老师让学生用不同的语调读同一句话，提醒道：Try an expressive reading, not a flat one.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「富有表现力、能清楚传达情绪的」（第 1 个义项：把情感或意义有力地传达出来）；句意为老师让学生读得有表现力，而不是平铺直叙。

pos.zh: 富于表现力的；表情丰富的；意味深长的

senses.title: Clearly conveying feeling or meaning
senses.titleCN: 清楚传达情感或意义的
senses.definition: communicating feeling or meaning in a strong and clear way
senses.definitionCN: 以强烈而清楚的方式传达情感或意义
senses.example: She gave an expressive performance of the song.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这首歌唱得极富表现力。
senses.why: The suffix means 'having the quality of', and the root action is pressing out, so the word describes something that lets feeling come out strongly.
senses.whyCN: 后缀意为「具有……性质的」，词根动作是「压出」，因此这个词形容能把情感强烈释放出来的事物。

senses.title: A face or eyes that show emotion
senses.titleCN: 脸部或眼睛显露情绪的
senses.definition: showing emotion openly through facial features or the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 通过面部特征或眼神公开显示情感
senses.example: His expressive eyes gave him away before he spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没开口，会说话的眼睛就出卖了他。
senses.why: The face is the most direct surface for expression, so an expressive face is one where the inner state is easy to read.
senses.whyCN: 脸是表达最直接的表面，因此「表情丰富的脸」就是内心状态容易被读出的脸。

senses.title: Emotionally powerful art or music
senses.titleCN: 情感力量强烈的艺术或音乐
senses.definition: full of emotional force in performance, sound or visual form
senses.definitionCN: 在表演、声音或视觉形式中充满情感力量
senses.example: The cello line is quietly expressive.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴的旋律线含蓄而富有表现力。
senses.why: Art can press feeling out through shape and sound, so the same adjective applies to a painting or a phrase of music.
senses.whyCN: 艺术能通过形状与声音把情感压出，因此同一个形容词也适用于绘画或一段音乐。

senses.title: Precise and vivid language
senses.definition: using words in a way that carries a vivid impression
senses.definitionCN: 用词能带来鲜明印象的
senses.example: An expressive phrase can carry a whole scene.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生动的短语就能承载整个场景。
senses.why: When words are chosen so that meaning comes out sharply, the language itself is called expressive.
senses.whyCN: 当词语被选到让意义鲜明地出来时，语言本身就被称为富有表现力。

senses.title: Attitude meaning in linguistics
senses.titleCN: 语言学中表达态度的意义
senses.definition: in linguistics, carrying the speaker's emotion or attitude rather than plain reference
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，携带说话人的情感或态度，而非单纯指称
senses.example: Expressive meaning includes surprise, affection and irritation.
senses.exampleCN: 表达性意义包括惊讶、喜爱与恼怒。
senses.why: Language has a layer that shows how the speaker feels about what is said, and that layer is called expressive.
senses.whyCN: 语言有一层显示说话人对所述内容感受的成分，这一层被称为表达性的。

senses.title: Meaningful gesture or movement
senses.titleCN: 意味深长的手势或动作
senses.definition: conveying meaning through bodily movement rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 通过身体动作而不是词语传达意义
senses.example: Her expressive hands shaped the idea in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的双手在空中把那个想法塑了出来。
senses.why: Hands can press a meaning into space, which is why a gesture can be described with the same word as a face.
senses.whyCN: 双手能把意义压进空间里，因此一个手势也能用与脸相同的词来形容。

senses.title: Full of character in style or design
senses.titleCN: 风格或设计上个性鲜明的
senses.definition: having a strong and distinctive character in form or style
senses.definitionCN: 在形式或风格上有强烈而独特个性的
senses.example: The building's expressive roof divides opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑个性鲜明的屋顶让人评价两极。
senses.why: Design can also push an attitude outward, so a bold shape may be called expressive even without words.
senses.whyCN: 设计也能把一种态度向外推出，因此大胆的形状即使没有词语也可称为有表现力。

senses.title: Serving as a sign of something
senses.definition: acting as a visible sign of a quality, feeling or fact
senses.definitionCN: 作为某种品质、情感或事实的可见标志
senses.example: The vote was expressive of public anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那次投票体现了公众的愤怒。
senses.why: The construction with 'of' turns the adjective into a pointer: the visible thing shows what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 与表示「关于」的介词连用时，这个形容词变成指针：可见之物显示出它背后的东西。

intro.en: Expressive joins express, from Latin exprimere 'to press out', with the Latin suffix -ivus, which marks a tendency or quality. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expressive 由 express（源自拉丁语 exprimere「压出」）加拉丁语形容词后缀构成，该后缀标记倾向或性质。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere 'to press' gave exprimere, whose senses included squeezing out and representing in words or art.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere「压」构成 exprimere，其意义包括挤出，以及用词语或艺术表现。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives of tendency or quality, as in words describing what something tends to do or is full of.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀构成表示倾向或性质的形容词，用来描述某物倾向于做什么或充满什么。

items.en: English expressive appears in the sixteenth century as the adjective of expression, first in the sense of serving to express.
items.cn: 英语 expressive 在十六世纪出现，作为 expression 的形容词，最初表示「用于表达的」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it had acquired the stronger sense 'full of expression, vivid, showing feeling clearly'.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它获得了更强的意义「充满表现力、生动、清楚显示情感」。

items.en: Later applications extend to art, music, design and linguistics, where the word labels emotional or attitudinal meaning.
items.cn: 后来的用法扩展到艺术、音乐、设计与语言学，在这些领域标记情感或态度意义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains unsettled, so proposed root forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：确切的最早书证没有定论，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，因此提出的词根形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds morphological neighbours that differ by prefix or suffix; group two holds near synonyms for vivid showing.
note.cn: 第一组是靠前缀或后缀区分开的构词近邻；第二组是表示「鲜明显示」的近义词。

entries.definition: With 'in' rather than 'out': it describes something that presses a strong effect into the mind, not something that shows feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：形容某物把强烈效果压进心里，而不是显示情感。

entries.definition: The suffix means 'can be': it says that something is capable of being put into words, not that it is vivid.
entries.definitionCN: 后缀意为「能够被」：表示某事可以被用词语说出来，而不是生动。

entries.definition: It describes an art style that gives an impression of a scene; the inward prefix marks it as a cousin rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一种给人场景印象的艺术风格；向内的前缀表明它是同族而非同义词。

entries.definition: It is the direct opposite: a face or performance that shows no feeling at all.
entries.definitionCN: 它是直接的反面：完全不显示情感的脸或表演。

entries.definition: It stresses fluent, persuasive speech; expressive can apply to a face, a sound or a design.
entries.definitionCN: 强调流利而有说服力的言辞；expressive 可用于脸、声音或设计。

entries.definition: It describes something that produces a strong mental image; expressive focuses on the feeling being pushed outward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容能产生强烈心理画面的东西；expressive 聚焦于被向外推出的情感。

entries.definition: It means causing emotion in the audience; expressive means full of emotion that is being shown.
entries.definitionCN: 意为在观众身上激起情感；expressive 意为充满并显示情感。

entries.definition: It stresses the successful passing of information; expressive stresses the force and feeling of the display.
entries.definitionCN: 强调信息成功传递；expressive 强调展示的力量与情感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the suffix of quality, the outward root and the real domains of use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示性质的后缀、向外的词根与真实的使用领域。

normal.en: The suffix means 'having the quality of', so expressive means having the quality of pressing feeling out.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「具有……性质」，因此这个词意为具有把情感压出来的性质。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing is expressive, inward pressing is impressive.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压是「有表现力」，向内压是「给人深刻印象」。

normal.en: Three domains: an expressive face, an expressive line of music, an expressive phrase.
normal.cn: 三个领域：表情丰富的脸、富有表现力的乐句、生动的短语。

normal.en: The opposite is built with the suffix meaning 'without'.
normal.cn: 反义词由表示「没有」的后缀构成。

normal.en: Linguistics uses the word for the layer of language that shows the speaker's attitude.
normal.cn: 语言学用这个词指语言中显示说话人态度的层次。

abstract.en: Picture a face that tells the whole story before a single word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸在一个字说出之前就讲完了整个故事。

abstract.en: Picture a melody that makes the room go quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一段旋律让整个房间安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a gesture so clear that it needs no translation.
abstract.cn: 想象一个清楚到不需要翻译的手势。

examples.en: The actor's expressive face carried the silent scene.
examples.cn: 演员表情丰富的脸撑起了那场无声的戏。

examples.en: Her letter was expressive of gratitude rather than apology.
examples.cn: 她的信体现的是感激，而不是歉意。

examples.en: The dialect uses expressive particles to show surprise.
examples.cn: 这种方言用表达性小品词来表示惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有表现力的」——把心里的情绪压到脸上、声音里 → 表情丰富的

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」的过去分词词干加拉丁形容词后缀；前缀表「向外」，词根 premere 表「压」。premere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one quality to different surfaces: performance, face, art, language, attitude, gesture, design and visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种性质用到不同表面：表演、脸、艺术、语言、态度、手势、设计与可见标志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feeling is pushed out so strongly that others can read it at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：情感被强烈地推出来，别人一眼就能读到。

branches.en: GENERAL QUALITY: the broad claim that something conveys feeling or meaning clearly.
branches.cn: 一般性质：某物能清楚传达情感或意义的宽泛判断。

branches.en: FACE: the surface where emotion is easiest to read.
branches.cn: 脸：情绪最容易被读出的表面。

branches.en: ART AND GESTURE: sound and bodily movement both shape feeling in visible or audible form.
branches.cn: 艺术与手势：声音与身体动作都把情感塑成可见或可听的形式。

branches.en: LANGUAGE LAYERS: vivid wording and the speaker's attitude both add feeling to plain reference.
branches.cn: 语言层次：生动的措辞与说话人的态度都给单纯指称添上情感。

branches.en: DESIGN AND SIGN: a bold form and a visible indication both point beyond themselves.
branches.cn: 设计与标志：大胆的形式与可见的指示都指向自身之外。

intro.en: Expressive is the adjective of quality built on the pressing verb, and its suffix can be compared with the suffixes of its neighbours.
intro.cn: expressive 是在表示「压」的动词上构成的性质形容词，它的后缀可以与邻近词的后缀相比较。

latinIntro.en: Latin exprimere supplies the root; -ivus supplies the sense 'tending to or full of', and English adds -ly and -ness for the adverb and noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exprimere 提供词根；形容词后缀提供「倾向于或充满」的意义，英语再加副词后缀与名词后缀构成新词。

items.example: The face can express what speech hides.
items.exampleCN: 脸能表达言语所隐藏的东西。

items.meaning: tending to; having the quality of
items.example: The suffix turns an action into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成性质。

items.example: Her expressive voice held the audience.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的嗓音抓住了听众。

items.meaning: in a way that shows feeling
items.example: He read the line expressively.
items.exampleCN: 他富有表现力地读了那一行。

items.example: The dancer's expressiveness silenced the hall.
items.exampleCN: 舞者的表现力让全场安静下来。

items.meaning: the act or result of showing
items.example: The painting is an expression of grief.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是悲伤的表达。

items.example: His inexpressive reply concealed his anger.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无表情的回应掩盖了怒气。

items.example: The scale of the bridge is impressive.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥的规模令人印象深刻。

items.meaning: able to be put into words
items.example: The feeling was real but hardly expressible.
items.exampleCN: 那种感受很真实，却几乎无法用语言表达。

definition_zh: 精美的；精致的；剧烈的；敏锐的；讲究的
definition_en: delicately beautiful because it is finely made or carefully chosen; also used of very sharp feeling and intense pain or pleasure
core_image: 匠人把一捧瓷片摊在案上，只留下最薄最亮的一片，反复打磨到透光
scene: 老匠人把一只薄胎瓷碗举到窗边，光从碗壁透了过来。The bowl is exquisite, so thin that light passes through its walls.
sceneCN: 这里 exquisite 是「精美的」（第 1 个义项：做工精细、样子秀美）；句意：这只碗精美绝伦，薄得光都能透过去。

pos.zh: 精美的；精致的；剧烈的；敏锐的；讲究的

senses.title: Finely made and beautiful
senses.definition: made with great care and skill, so that it looks delicate and beautiful
senses.definitionCN: 做工精细、技艺高超，因而显得秀美雅致
senses.example: She wore an exquisite silk gown embroidered with silver thread.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着一件用银线绣成的精美丝质长裙。
senses.why: The Latin participle means sought out: the maker has searched through many possibilities and kept only the best material and the finest finish.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词意为「被寻求出来的」：匠人翻检许多可能，只留下最好的材料与最细的做工。

senses.title: Intensely felt
senses.definition: of pain or pleasure: felt very sharply and deeply
senses.definitionCN: 指疼痛或快乐：感受极其尖锐、深切
senses.example: A sudden exquisite pain shot through his wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵剧烈的疼痛突然穿过他的手腕。
senses.why: What is picked out from everything else is also sharp and unmixed; the same word names a feeling that stands out above all others.
senses.whyCN: 从万物中被挑出来的东西也最纯粹、最尖锐；同一个词因此也指一种盖过其他一切的感觉。

senses.title: Keenly perceptive
senses.definition: showing a very delicate ability to notice small differences, especially in taste or hearing
senses.definitionCN: 表现出能察觉细微差别的细腻能力，尤指品味或听觉
senses.example: Her exquisite ear caught the slight flat note in the choir.
senses.exampleCN: 她敏锐的耳朵听出了合唱里那个略微走音的音符。
senses.why: Selection requires discrimination: to choose the best you must notice the smallest differences, so the word grows into keen and discriminating.
senses.whyCN: 挑选需要分辨力：要选出最好的，就得察觉最细小的差别，于是这个词长出「敏锐、有鉴别力」的意思。

senses.title: Refined and elegant
senses.definition: showing refined manners, style, or taste that please highly cultivated people
senses.definitionCN: 举止、风格或品味高雅，令有教养的人十分欣赏
senses.example: The hotel is known for its exquisite service and quiet elegance.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店以优雅的服务和安静的格调著称。
senses.why: The object chosen for its quality becomes a standard of taste; a person or service that meets that standard is also called exquisite.
senses.whyCN: 因品质而被选中的物件成了品味标准；达到这一标准的人或服务也被称为 exquisite。

senses.title: Carefully chosen, choice
senses.definition: selected with care from among many, and therefore of the highest quality
senses.definitionCN: 从许多当中仔细选出，因而品质极高
senses.example: The shop sells exquisite teas brought from small mountain gardens.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售从高山小茶园运来的上等茶叶。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: exquirere means to search out thoroughly, and exquisitus is the thing that has survived that search.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：exquirere 意为彻底搜寻，exquisitus 就是经受过这番搜寻而留下来的东西。

senses.title: Fastidious, overnice
senses.definition: of a person: too careful about small matters of dress, food, or comfort
senses.definitionCN: 指人：对衣着、饮食或舒适等小事过分讲究
senses.example: The exquisite young man complained about the least crease in his collar.
senses.exampleCN: 那个过分讲究的年轻人连衣领上最轻的折痕都要抱怨。
senses.why: Carried too far, the habit of selecting only the best turns into fussiness; English once used exquisite for a dandy.
senses.whyCN: 把只选最好的习惯推过头，就变成挑剔；英语早期曾用 exquisite 指打扮讲究的花花公子。

senses.title: Subtle, barely noticeable
senses.definition: so slight or delicate that it is hard to notice or describe
senses.definitionCN: 极其轻微或细微，难以察觉或描述
senses.example: There is an exquisite difference between the two shades of grey.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种灰色之间有一种微妙的差别。
senses.why: A difference that only a trained eye can pick out is itself sought out; delicacy of perception passes into delicacy of the thing perceived.
senses.whyCN: 只有受过训练的眼睛才能挑出的差别，本身也是「被搜寻出来的」；感知的细腻延伸为被感知之物的细微。

intro.en: Exquisite comes from Latin exquisitus, the past participle of exquirere, to seek out, from ex- out and quaerere to seek. English first used it of something carefully selected, then of delicate beauty, and later of very intense feeling.
intro.cn: exquisite 来自拉丁语 exquisitus，是 exquirere（彻底寻求）的过去分词，由 ex-（出）与 quaerere（寻求）构成。英语先用它指「精挑细选的上等之物」，再引申为「精致秀美」，后来又指「感受强烈」。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or hunt for something. The image is active: a person goes out looking, not merely owning.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问、追索。意象是主动的：人走出去寻找，而不是坐着拥有。

items.en: Exquirere adds ex- out and means to search something out thoroughly, until the right thing is found.
items.cn: exquirere 加上 ex-「出」，意为把某物彻底搜寻出来，直到找到合意的那一件。

items.en: Exquisitus, the past participle, describes what has survived that search: choice, select, excellent.
items.cn: 过去分词 exquisitus 描述经受过这番搜寻而留下来的东西：精选的、上等的、优异的。

items.en: English borrows the adjective in the fifteenth century with the sense carefully selected and of fine quality.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，义为「精挑细选的、品质上乘的」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it describes delicate beauty and keen feeling; modern English adds intense pain and pleasure.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它已描写精致的美与敏锐的感觉；现代英语又加上剧烈的疼痛与极度的快乐。

note.en: The first group shares the quaerere root or the exquisite family; the second group holds words for fine beauty and intensity nearby.
note.cn: 第一组共享 quaerere 词根或 exquisite 词族；第二组是与精美、强烈感受相邻的词。

entries.definition: in a finely made or delicate way
the quality of being exquisite
curious and eager to ask questions
entries.definitionCN: 好奇的；爱刨根问底的（与 quaerere 同根）

entries.definition: finely made and easily damaged
showing polished good taste
graceful and stylish in appearance or manner

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real quaerere root, the word family, and the phrases exquisite actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 quaerere 词根、同族词，以及 exquisite 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ex- means out and quaerere means seek: exquisite is the thing that has been searched out and kept.
normal.cn: ex- 意为「出」，quaerere 意为「寻求」：exquisite 就是被搜寻出来并留下来的东西。

normal.en: The same quaerere root gives inquisitive, query and requisite, all about asking or seeking.
normal.cn: 同一 quaerere 词根还给出 inquisitive、query、requisite，都与询问或寻求有关。

normal.en: Exquisitely carved and exquisite craftsmanship are the everyday collocations for fine work.
normal.cn: exquisitely carved 与 exquisite craftsmanship 是形容精细做工的常用搭配。

normal.en: Exquisite pain and exquisite pleasure use the word for feeling that is sharp and unmixed.
normal.cn: exquisite pain 与 exquisite pleasure 用这个词形容尖锐而纯粹的感受。

normal.en: Delicate can mean easily broken; exquisite stresses that the thing was chosen and finished with care.
normal.cn: delicate 可以指容易损坏；exquisite 则强调这件东西经过精心挑选与打磨。

abstract.en: Picture a potter laying out a heap of thin clay shards and keeping only the one that lets the light through.
abstract.cn: 想象陶匠摊开一堆薄瓷片，只留下那片能让光透过的。

abstract.en: Think of a needle so fine that the pain it makes is sharp but perfectly clear.
abstract.cn: 想象一根极细的针，扎出的疼痛尖锐却清清楚楚。

abstract.en: See an ear pressed close to a string, catching a half note that others miss.
abstract.cn: 想象一只耳朵贴近琴弦，捕捉到别人漏掉的半音。

examples.en: The museum owns an exquisite clock made for a seventeenth-century duke.
examples.cn: 博物馆藏有一座为十七世纪公爵制作的精美时钟。

examples.en: She has exquisite taste in fabrics and never buys anything coarse.
examples.cn: 她对布料有高雅的品味，从不买粗糙的东西。

examples.en: The tea was so exquisite that the guests asked where it came from.
examples.cn: 这茶如此精美，客人们都问它是从哪里来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊克斯奎齐特」：像在旧货市场里翻找，翻到最后才捧出那件最精美的；只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（出）+ quaerere（寻求）→ exquirere（彻底寻求）→ 过去分词 exquisitus（被挑选出来的、上等的）→ 英语 exquisite；核心义「从众多中挑出的精品」。

sensesIntro.en: Exquisite starts from the thing searched out and chosen, then moves to delicate beauty, then to the keen senses that notice it, and finally to feelings that are equally sharp.
sensesIntro.cn: exquisite 从「被搜寻出来并选中的东西」出发，转向精致的美，再转向能察觉这种美的敏锐感官，最后转向同样尖锐的感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one flawless piece kept after a long search.
core.cn: 核心意象：翻检许多之后留下的那一片无瑕之作。

branches.en: The chosen piece and the finely made object are the same promise of quality made visible.
branches.cn: 被选中的材料与做工精细的物件，是同一个品质承诺的可见形态。

branches.en: Intensity is the emotional version of a thing that stands out from everything else.
branches.cn: 强度是「从一切事物中凸显出来」在情感上的版本。

branches.en: Keen perception is the search turned inward, into the senses.
branches.cn: 敏锐的感知是搜寻转向内部、进入感官的结果。

branches.en: Refined manners are beauty transferred from the object to the person.
branches.cn: 优雅的举止是把美从物件转移到人身上。

branches.en: Fussiness and subtlety are the two edges of the same delicacy: too much attention, or the smallest difference.
branches.cn: 过分讲究与微妙是同一份细腻的两端：注意力过多，或差别极小。

intro.en: Exquisite is built on the Latin verb quaerere, to seek, with the prefix ex-, out. The family includes exquisitely, exquisiteness, and the same-root inquisitive and requisite.
intro.cn: exquisite 建立在拉丁语动词 quaerere（寻求）与前缀 ex-（向外）之上；同族词包括 exquisitely、exquisiteness，以及同根的 inquisitive 与 requisite。

latinIntro.en: Latin exquirere means to seek out thoroughly; its participle exquisitus gives English exquisite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exquirere 意为彻底寻求；它的分词 exquisitus 给出英语 exquisite。

items.example: The prefix turns seeking into seeking out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「寻求」变成「寻求出来」。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of question and query.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 question 与 query 的词根。

items.example: Exquirere adds the idea of a thorough search.
items.exampleCN: exquirere 加上了彻底搜寻的意思。

items.example: Exquisitus describes the best of what was found.
items.exampleCN: exquisitus 描述所找到之物中最好的那部分。

items.example: Exquisite names the chosen quality.
items.exampleCN: exquisite 命名那种被挑选出的品质。

items.example: The box was exquisitely carved.
items.exampleCN: 盒子雕刻得十分精美。

items.example: The exquisiteness of the work needs close looking.
items.exampleCN: 这件作品的精美需要凑近细看。

items.example: Inquisitive keeps the quaerere sense of asking.
items.exampleCN: inquisitive 保留了 quaerere 的「询问」义。

items.example: Requisite is what has been sought and is needed.
items.exampleCN: requisite 是被寻求过、并且确实需要的东西。

items.example: Query comes from quaerere through French.
items.exampleCN: query 经由法语来自 quaerere。

definition_zh: 现存的；尚存的；留传至今的；现行的；残存的
definition_en: still in existence, especially after a long time or when most others have disappeared
core_image: 大火过后，整条街只剩一堵旧墙还立在原地
scene: 旧城清拆后，整条街只剩下那座小教堂还站在原地。Only that small church is still extant on the cleared street.
sceneCN: 这里 extant 是「现存的」（第 1 个义项：至今仍然存在）；句意：清拆后的街上，只有那座小教堂还留在原地。

pos.zh: 现存的；尚存的；留传至今的；现行的；残存的

derivatives.zh: 不存在的；已失传的（多用于书目与文物描述）

senses.title: Still in existence
senses.titleCN: 现存的（建筑、文件、艺术品）
senses.definition: still in existence, especially of a building, document, or work of art that has survived from an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 仍然存在，尤指从较早时期留存下来的建筑、文件或艺术品
senses.example: The oldest extant copy of the poem dates from the ninth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗现存最古老的抄本可追溯到九世纪。
senses.why: Extant is the present participle of a Latin verb meaning to stand out; what stands out is still visible, and what is still visible still exists.
senses.whyCN: extant 是拉丁语动词「站出、显露」的现在分词；站得出来的东西仍然可见，仍然可见的东西就仍然存在。

senses.title: Surviving, not extinct
senses.definition: of a species, language, or custom: still living or in use, not extinct
senses.definitionCN: 指物种、语言或习俗仍然存活或仍在使用，并未灭绝
senses.example: Several extant species of frog live only in the cloud forest.
senses.exampleCN: 有几种尚存的蛙只生活在云雾林里。
senses.why: The same standing image applies to living things: a species that has not fallen is still standing among us.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「站立」意象也用于生物：没有倒下的物种，就还站在我们中间。

senses.title: Preserved from the past
senses.definition: preserved from an earlier period and still available to be seen or read
senses.definitionCN: 从较早时期保存下来、至今仍可见可读的
senses.example: Few extant photographs show the bridge before the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 留存至今的照片里，很少拍到了火灾之前的这座桥。
senses.why: Survival is selective: most things are lost, so the extant ones are the few that stood through time.
senses.whyCN: 留存是有选择性的：大多数东西都散失了，所以 extant 之物就是经受住时间、一直站到今天的少数。

senses.title: Currently in force
senses.definition: of a law, rule, or system: currently in force or still operating
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、规则或制度目前有效、仍在运行
senses.example: Under extant law, the council must publish the minutes within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 根据现行法律，市议会必须在一个月内公布会议记录。
senses.why: A law that is extant has not been repealed: it still stands on the statute book.
senses.whyCN: extant 的法律没有被废止：它仍然「立」在法令全书中。

senses.title: Remaining in traces
senses.definition: remaining in only a few traces, examples, or places
senses.definitionCN: 只剩少量痕迹、实例或地点而继续存在
senses.example: Extant traces of the old wall can still be seen in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 旧墙残存的痕迹仍能在地窖里看到。
senses.why: What remains may be only a fragment, but a fragment still stands; the word covers the last visible part of something larger.
senses.whyCN: 留下来的也许只是残片，但残片仍然立着；这个词涵盖了某件更大事物最后可见的部分。

intro.en: Extant comes from Latin exstare, to stand out or be visible, from ex- out and stare to stand. English borrowed the present participle directly in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: extant 来自拉丁语 exstare（站出来、可见），由 ex-（出）与 stare（站立）构成。英语在十七世纪直接借用了它的现在分词。

items.en: Stare means to stand, to stand still, or to remain in place. The root also gives station and stable.
items.cn: stare 意为站立、站定或留在原地。同一词根还给出 station 与 stable。

items.en: Exstare adds ex- out: to stand out, to show oneself, and therefore to be visibly there.
items.cn: exstare 加上 ex-「出」：站到外面、显露自己，因而就是可见地存在着。

items.en: The present participle exstans, genitive exstantis, means standing out or being visible.
items.cn: 现在分词 exstans（属格 exstantis）意为「站出来的、可见的」。

items.en: Borrowed directly from Latin in the 1640s, extant first means still existing, especially of what has survived from the past.
items.cn: 十七世纪四十年代直接从拉丁语借入，extant 最初意为「仍然存在的」，尤指从过去留存下来的东西。

items.en: Modern use narrows to documents, species, buildings and laws: the few things that still stand.
items.cn: 现代用法收窄到文件、物种、建筑与法律：那些仍然立着的少数事物。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stare root, to stand; the second group holds words for what still exists or has survived.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语 stare（站立）词根；第二组是与「仍然存在、幸存下来」相关的词。

entries.definition: standing firm and unchanging
entries.definitionCN: 持续的；不变的（con- 加 stare，同根）

entries.definition: the space between two points
a moment, or happening at once
entries.definitionCN: 瞬间；即刻的（in- 加 stare，同根）

entries.definition: present now
still alive or present after others have gone
left over after others are gone

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real stare root, the standing image, and the phrases extant actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 stare 词根、「站立」意象，以及 extant 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Stare means to stand: ex- plus stare gives the idea of standing out into view.
normal.cn: stare 意为站立：ex- 加 stare 就是「站到外面、进入视野」。

normal.en: Something extant has stood out of the past and is still visible in the present.
normal.cn: extant 之物从过去站出来，至今仍然可见。

normal.en: Constant, distance, instant and substance all carry the same stare root.
normal.cn: constant、distance、instant、substance 都带着同一个 stare 词根。

normal.en: Extant manuscripts, extant species and still extant are the common collocations.
normal.cn: extant manuscripts、extant species 与 still extant 是常见搭配。

normal.en: Contrast extinct: what is extant still stands, while what is extinct has been stamped out.
normal.cn: 对比 extinct：extant 的东西仍然立着，extinct 的东西则已被扑灭。

abstract.en: Picture one old wall left standing after every house on the street has been pulled down.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街的房子都被推倒后，只剩一堵旧墙还立着。

abstract.en: See the last two birds of a kind still building a nest on a small island.
abstract.cn: 想象某一类鸟只剩最后两只，仍在小岛上筑巢。

abstract.en: Think of a worm-eaten sheet taken from the bottom of a chest, its ink still readable.
abstract.cn: 想象从箱底取出一张虫蛀的旧纸，上面的字迹仍能辨认。

examples.en: The library holds the only extant copy of that 1631 pamphlet.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆藏有那本一六三一年小册子唯一现存的副本。

examples.en: Extant species of frog live only in the cloud forest.
examples.cn: 尚存的蛙类只生活在云雾林里。

examples.en: The rule is no longer extant, but old signs still quote it.
examples.cn: 这条规则已不再现行，但旧告示上还引着它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊克斯坦特」：像一份旧档案还在架子上，没有被销毁；只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（出）+ stare（站立）→ exstare（站出来、显露、存在）→ 现在分词 exstans（站出来的、存在的）→ 英语 extant；核心义「还立在那里」。

sensesIntro.en: Extant moves from the general fact of still existing to the survival of species, of old objects, of laws, and finally to the last traces of what is almost gone.
sensesIntro.cn: extant 从「仍然存在」这一总事实出发，依次走向物种的存活、旧物的留存、法律的现行，最后是几乎消失之物留下的残迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one old wall still standing after the street around it is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：周围街道都已消失，只剩一堵旧墙还立着。

branches.en: A building or document that still stands is the plainest sense of extant.
branches.cn: 仍然立着的建筑或文件，是 extant 最朴素的义项。

branches.en: A species that has not fallen still stands among the living.
branches.cn: 没有倒下的物种，仍然立在生物之中。

branches.en: Old objects survive selectively, so the extant ones are the few that time spared.
branches.cn: 旧物有选择地留存，所以 extant 之物是时间放过的少数。

branches.en: A law still on the books is extant because it has not been repealed.
branches.cn: 仍留在法令全书上的法律之所以是现行的，是因为它没有被废止。

branches.en: A trace is the last standing part of something nearly gone.
branches.cn: 残迹是几乎消失之物最后仍立着的那一部分。

intro.en: Extant is built on Latin stare, to stand, with ex-, out. The same standing root appears in constant, distance, instant and substance.
intro.cn: extant 建立在拉丁语 stare（站立）与前缀 ex-（向外）之上；同一个「站立」词根还出现在 constant、distance、instant 与 substance 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin exstare means to stand out, be visible, and therefore to exist; the participle exstans gives English extant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exstare 意为站出来、可见，因而也就是存在；分词 exstans 给出英语 extant。

items.example: The prefix moves standing into view.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「站立」移到可见之处。

items.example: Stare is the standing root of the family.
items.exampleCN: stare 是这个词族的「站立」词根。

items.meaning: to stand out, be visible, exist
items.example: Exstare links visibility with existence.
items.exampleCN: exstare 把可见与存在连在一起。

items.example: Exstans is the participle behind extant.
items.exampleCN: exstans 是 extant 背后的分词。

items.example: Extant describes what still stands.
items.exampleCN: extant 描述仍然立着的东西。

items.example: Nonextant marks a lost manuscript.
items.exampleCN: nonextant 标记一部已失传的手稿。

items.example: Extantness is rare but transparent.
items.exampleCN: extantness 罕用，但意思一目了然。

items.example: Constant joins con- with stare.

definition_zh: 即兴的；无准备的；临时的；即席的
definition_en: spoken, performed, or made without preparation, on the spur of the moment
core_image: 台上的人手里没有稿子，张口就讲，边讲边想
scene: 礼堂里话筒突然递到学生手里，他愣了一下便开口讲了起来。The student gave an extemporaneous speech that held the hall silent.
sceneCN: 这里 extemporaneous 是「即兴的」（第 1 个义项：没有事先准备、当场说出或做出）；句意：那名学生做了一场即兴演讲，全场安静。

pos.zh: 即兴的；无准备的；临时的；即席的

senses.title: Spoken without preparation
senses.definition: spoken or delivered without notes or previous preparation, especially before an audience
senses.definitionCN: 没有稿子、也没有事先准备就说出或发表，尤指面对听众
senses.example: Her extemporaneous answer was clearer than the prepared slides.
senses.exampleCN: 她即兴的回答比准备好的幻灯片还清楚。
senses.why: The Latin phrase is ex tempore, out of time: speech made when there is no time left to write it down.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语短语是 ex tempore，意为「在时间之外」：没有时间先写下来，就只能当场说。

senses.title: Arranged at the last moment
senses.titleCN: 临时凑成的：没有事先准备
senses.definition: arranged or done at the moment because there was no time to prepare
senses.definitionCN: 因为没有时间准备而在当下安排或完成
senses.example: The dinner was extemporaneous, put together from whatever the fridge held.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿饭是临时凑成的，冰箱里有什么就做什么。
senses.why: If no time was set aside beforehand, the thing has to be arranged in the moment; the word moves from speech to any last-minute arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有事先留出时间，事情就只能在当下安排；这个词于是从说话扩展到一切临时安排。

senses.title: Invented in performance
senses.definition: created and performed at the same moment, especially in music or drama
senses.definitionCN: 在同一时刻创作并表演，尤指音乐或戏剧
senses.example: The pianist closed the concert with an extemporaneous piece built on a folk tune.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家以一首根据民谣即席创作的小曲结束了音乐会。
senses.why: Music makes the moment audible: notes are chosen as they sound, not before.
senses.whyCN: 音乐让当下变得可听：音符在响起的同时被选出，而不是在此之前。

senses.title: Written on the spot
senses.definition: composed in writing on the spot, without drafting or planning
senses.definitionCN: 当场写成的，没有草稿或事先构思
senses.example: He wrote an extemporaneous poem on the back of the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 他在节目单背面即兴写了一首诗。
senses.why: Writing can also be done out of time, with the line composed as the pen moves.
senses.whyCN: 写作同样可以在时间之外完成：句子随着笔尖移动而被组织出来。

senses.title: Worked out during the event
senses.definition: worked out during the event itself, as in a debate or a match
senses.definitionCN: 在事件进行当中才想出来并执行，如辩论或比赛
senses.example: The debater relied on extemporaneous rebuttal rather than a written case.
senses.exampleCN: 辩手依靠临场反驳，而不是照念写好的立论。
senses.why: Under pressure the plan must be made during the event, so the word covers live adjustment as well.
senses.whyCN: 在压力之下，计划只能在事件进行中形成，于是这个词也涵盖现场调整。

intro.en: Extemporaneous comes from Latin extemporaneus, made without preparation, from ex- out of and tempus time. Literally it means out of time: the speaker had no time to prepare.
intro.cn: extemporaneous 来自拉丁语 extemporaneus（无准备而做成），由 ex-（出）与 tempus（时间）构成。字面意思是「在时间之外」：说话者没有时间准备。

items.en: Tempus means time, with the genitive temporis. The root also gives temporary, contemporary and tempo.
items.cn: tempus 意为时间，属格是 temporis。同一词根还给出 temporary、contemporary 与 tempo。

items.en: The phrase ex tempore means out of time, or without time to prepare: something done on the spot.
items.cn: 短语 ex tempore 意为「在时间之外」，也就是没有准备时间：当场做成的事。

items.en: Extemporaneus turns that phrase into an adjective for a speech or act made on the spur of the moment.
items.cn: extemporaneus 把这个短语变成形容词，指一时兴起、当场做出的言语或行为。

items.en: Extempore entered English in the 1540s; extemporaneous is recorded in the 1660s, first for speech delivered without notes.
items.cn: extempore 于十六世纪四十年代进入英语；extemporaneous 记录于十七世纪六十年代，最初指不带稿子的发言。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word for speech, performance and writing, while extemporary and extemporize extend the family.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词保留给演讲、表演与写作，同时由 extemporary 与 extemporize 扩展词族。

note.en: The first group is the same tempus family; the second group is the nearby vocabulary of improvisation.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 tempus 的词族；第二组是即兴、现场发挥一类的近义词。

entries.definition: spoken or performed without preparation
entries.definitionCN: 即兴的；即席的（直接来自拉丁短语 ex tempore）

entries.definition: made or done on the spot
entries.definitionCN: 即兴的；临时的（与 extemporaneous 同族）

entries.definition: to perform or speak without preparation
entries.definitionCN: 即兴表演；当场创作（动词形式）

entries.definition: made or done without preparation, often on impulse
acting or happening naturally, without planning
made with whatever is available at the moment
entries.definitionCN: 临时拼凑的；即兴改编的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real tempus root, the phrase ex tempore, and the collocations extemporaneous actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 tempus 词根、ex tempore 短语，以及 extemporaneous 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ex- means out of and tempus means time: extemporaneous work is made out of time, with none to spare.
normal.cn: ex- 意为「出」，tempus 意为「时间」：extemporaneous 的作品是在时间之外做成的，一点余裕也没有。

normal.en: The Latin phrase ex tempore is the ancestor; extempore is its short English child.
normal.cn: 拉丁语短语 ex tempore 是祖先，extempore 是它在英语里的短小后代。

normal.en: Tempus also gives temporary, contemporary and tempo, all about time.
normal.cn: tempus 还给出 temporary、contemporary 与 tempo，全都与时间有关。

normal.en: Extemporaneous speech and extemporaneous remarks are the usual collocations.
normal.cn: extemporaneous speech 与 extemporaneous remarks 是常见搭配。

normal.en: Impromptu often suggests a short piece made on impulse; extemporaneous stresses that no preparation was possible, especially in speech.
normal.cn: impromptu 常指一时兴起做成的短作；extemporaneous 则强调根本来不及准备，尤指发言。

abstract.en: Picture an empty lectern, a microphone pushed into your hand, and words arriving as you speak.
abstract.cn: 想象讲台上空无一物，话筒被塞进你手里，话随着开口一句句到来。

abstract.en: See guests arriving early while the host assembles a meal from whatever the fridge holds.
abstract.cn: 想象客人提前进门，主人只能用冰箱里现有的东西凑出一桌饭。

abstract.en: Hear a jazz player inventing a melody against the drumbeat, never repeating a written line.
abstract.cn: 想象爵士乐手跟着鼓点现编旋律，从不重复写好的句子。

examples.en: Her extemporaneous answer was clearer than the prepared slides.
examples.cn: 她即兴的回答比准备好的幻灯片还清楚。

examples.en: The professor gave an extemporaneous lecture when the projector failed.
examples.cn: 投影仪坏掉时，教授做了一场即兴讲课。

examples.en: Jazz players value extemporaneous invention over note-perfect repetition.
examples.cn: 爵士乐手看重即兴创造，胜过一个音不差的重复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「伊克斯腾普」：临时腾出手就上台，没有稿子也能讲；只是声音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（出）+ tempus（时间，属格 temporis）→ ex tempore（在时间之外、没有时间准备）→ extemporaneus → 英语 extemporaneous；核心义「不在时间之内，当场生成」。

sensesIntro.en: Extemporaneous begins with speech made without notes, then spreads to any last-minute arrangement, to music invented in performance, to writing done on the spot, and to live adjustment under pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: extemporaneous 从「不带稿子的发言」开始，扩展到一切临时安排、演奏时当场作曲、落笔即成的写作，以及压力下的临场调整。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker with no notes and no time to write them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个既没有稿子、也没有时间写稿的说话者。

branches.en: A speech without notes is the first and most typical sense.
branches.cn: 不带稿子的发言，是这个词第一个、也最典型的义项。

branches.en: The same lack of time turns any arrangement into a last-minute one.
branches.cn: 同样的「没有时间」把任何安排都变成临时凑成。

branches.en: Music is the art where the making and the hearing happen together.
branches.cn: 音乐是创作与聆听同时发生的艺术。

branches.en: Writing without a draft repeats the pattern: the sentence is made as it appears.
branches.cn: 不打草稿的写作重复同一模式：句子在出现的同时被做成。

branches.en: A debate or match forces the plan itself to be made live, as the event unfolds.
branches.cn: 辩论或比赛迫使计划本身随着事件展开而在现场形成。

intro.en: Extemporaneous is built on Latin tempus, time, with ex-, out of. The family includes extempore, extemporary, extemporize, and the same-root contemporary and temporary.
intro.cn: extemporaneous 建立在拉丁语 tempus（时间）与前缀 ex-（出于）之上；同族词包括 extempore、extemporary、extemporize，以及同根的 contemporary 与 temporary。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex tempore means out of time, hence without preparation; extemporaneus turns the phrase into an adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex tempore 意为「在时间之外」，因而就是没有准备；extemporaneus 把这个短语变成形容词。

items.example: The prefix puts the action outside ordinary time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把行为放到寻常时间之外。

items.example: Tempus is the time root of the family.
items.exampleCN: tempus 是这个词族的时间词根。

items.meaning: out of time, on the spot
items.example: Ex tempore names speech made without preparation.
items.exampleCN: ex tempore 指没有准备而做出的发言。

items.example: Extemporaneus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: extemporaneus 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Extempore is the short English form.
items.exampleCN: extempore 是简短的英语形式。

items.example: Extemporary is the older adjective variant.
items.exampleCN: extemporary 是较早的形容词变体。

items.example: Extemporaneous is the full modern adjective.
items.exampleCN: extemporaneous 是完整的现代形容词。

items.example: He answered extemporaneously.
items.exampleCN: 他即兴作答。

items.meaning: to speak or perform without preparation
items.example: The actor had to extemporize when a prop broke.
items.exampleCN: 道具坏了，演员只好即兴发挥。

items.example: Contemporary joins con- with tempus.
items.exampleCN: contemporary 把 con- 与 tempus 结合在一起。

items.example: Temporary also comes from tempus.
items.exampleCN: temporary 同样来自 tempus。

definition_zh: 延伸；扩大；延长；给予
definition_en: to reach out over an area; to make longer or larger; to stretch out a hand; to offer help or an invitation
core_image: 一条路从脚下一直伸向远方的地平线
scene: 这条小路一直延伸到河边。The path extends to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 extend 是「延伸」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这条小路一直延伸到河边。

senses.title: Reach across space
senses.definition: to reach out or continue over an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某片区域上伸展或延续
senses.example: The forest extends for miles.
senses.exampleCN: 森林延伸数英里。
senses.why: The core sense is stretching out in space.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是在空间中向外伸展。

senses.title: Make longer or larger
senses.definition: to make something longer, larger, or later
senses.definitionCN: 使某物更长、更大或更晚
senses.example: They extended the meeting by an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议延长了一小时。
senses.why: Stretching in space becomes stretching in time or size.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的拉伸变成时间或规模上的延长。

senses.title: Stretch out a hand
senses.definition: to stretch out a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 伸出身体的某一部分
senses.example: He extended his hand in greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他伸出手来表示问候。
senses.why: The body repeats the outward stretch.
senses.whyCN: 身体重复了向外伸展的动作。

senses.title: Offer to someone
senses.definition: to offer help, thanks, or an invitation
senses.definitionCN: 给予帮助、感谢或邀请
senses.example: The school extended a warm welcome to us.
senses.exampleCN: 学校向我们表示了热烈欢迎。
senses.why: Reaching outward becomes offering something.
senses.whyCN: 向外伸手变成给出某物。

intro.en: Extend comes from Latin extendere, to stretch out, from ex- out and tendere to stretch.
intro.cn: extend 来自拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸），由 ex-（向外）与 tendere（拉）构成。

items.en: Ex- means out.
items.cn: ex- 意为向外。

items.en: Tendere means to stretch.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸。

items.en: Extendere means to stretch out.
items.cn: extendere 意为向外拉伸。

items.en: Extendre keeps the outward stretch.
items.cn: 古法语 extendre 保留向外伸展之义。

items.en: Extend covers space, time, and offers.
items.cn: 现代英语中 extend 涵盖空间、时间与给予。

note.en: Extend means stretch out; intend means plan.
note.cn: extend 是伸展开，intend 则是打算。

entries.definition: to plan to do something
to go to an event or place
to compete or argue
to make longer or wider
to make something longer
to become larger

normalIntro.en: Extend is the act of stretching something outward in space, time, or gesture.
normalIntro.cn: extend 是把事物在空间、时间或动作上向外伸展。

normal.en: The garden extends down to the lake.
normal.cn: 花园一直延伸到湖边。

normal.en: They extended the deadline by two days.
normal.cn: 他们把截止日期延长了两天。

normal.en: She extended her hand to help him up.
normal.cn: 她伸手把他扶起来。

normal.en: The company extended an offer to her.
normal.cn: 公司向她发出了聘用邀请。

normal.en: The shelf extends along the whole wall.
normal.cn: 架子沿着整面墙延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a road running straight to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路笔直伸向地平线。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand reaching across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过桌面。

abstract.en: Think of a calendar with extra days added.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上又添了几天。

examples.en: The desert extends far beyond the town.
examples.cn: 沙漠远远延伸到城镇之外。

examples.en: We extended the visit for another week.
examples.cn: 我们把访问又延长了一周。

examples.en: He extended his hand to the visitor.
examples.cn: 他向访客伸出了手。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（向外）加 tend（拉伸）：向外拉长，就是 extend（延伸、延长）。

root: 源自拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸），由 ex-（向外）与 tendere（拉）构成，核心义「向外伸展」。

sensesIntro.en: Extend means to reach across space, make longer or larger, stretch out a hand, or offer something.
sensesIntro.cn: extend 意为在空间中延伸、使更长更大、伸出手，或给予某物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road stretching to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸向地平线的一条路。

branches.en: The base sense is stretching across space.
branches.cn: 基础义是在空间中伸展。

branches.en: Stretching becomes longer time or larger size.
branches.cn: 伸展变成时间更长或规模更大。

branches.en: The body repeats the outward stretch.
branches.cn: 身体重复向外伸展的动作。

branches.en: Reaching out becomes giving or offering.
branches.cn: 向外伸出变成给予或提供。

branches.en: Spatial reach and temporal extension share one motion.
branches.cn: 空间延伸与时间延长共享同一动作。

intro.en: Extend belongs to the Latin tendere family, like extend, intend, and attend.
intro.cn: extend 属于拉丁语 tendere 词族，与 intend、attend 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin extendere, tendere, and the prefix ex- are the source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extendere、tendere 与前缀 ex- 是来源要素。

items.example: The line extends to the door.
items.exampleCN: 队伍一直延伸到门口。

items.example: The offer extends to all students.
items.exampleCN: 这项优惠面向所有学生。

items.example: They took an extended holiday.
items.exampleCN: 他们度了一个长假。

items.example: The extending road was empty.
items.exampleCN: 延伸的道路空无一人。

items.example: The visa needs an extension.
items.exampleCN: 签证需要延期。

items.example: The house has extensive gardens.
items.exampleCN: 这座房子有宽阔的花园。

items.meaning: the size or degree of something
items.example: The extent of the damage is unclear.
items.exampleCN: 损坏程度尚不清楚。

items.meaning: the state of being stretched tight
items.example: The rope was under tension.
items.exampleCN: 绳子处于拉紧状态。

items.meaning: a habit of moving or acting in one way
items.example: He has a tendency to arrive late.
items.exampleCN: 他有迟到的倾向。

definition_zh: 可延长的；可伸展的；可扩展的；可延期的
definition_en: able to be made longer, wider, or larger in scope, or able to be given more time
core_image: 一张桌面底下藏着一块木板，往外一拉，桌子立刻变长
scene: 摄影师把三脚架的支腿一节节往外抽，镜头才升到与阳台齐平的高度。The photographer pulled out the extendable legs of the tripod until the camera sat level with the balcony rail.
sceneCN: 这里 extendable 是「可伸展的」（第 2 个义项：部件能被抽出、拉长）；句意：摄影师把三脚架可伸长的支腿一节节抽出来，直到相机与阳台栏杆齐平。

pos.zh: 可延长的；可伸展的；可扩展的；可延期的

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「延长；扩展」
由 extend 加 -ion 构成，义为「延长；扩展；延期」
同根形容词，加 -ible 构成，义为「可伸长的；可扩展的」

senses.title: Able to be made longer
senses.definition: able to be made longer in physical length, especially by pulling out a leaf or adding an extra section
senses.definitionCN: 能在物理长度上变长，尤指抽出活动板或加上一节
senses.example: The dining table has an extendable leaf for family gatherings.
senses.exampleCN: 这张餐桌有一块可加长的活动板，供家庭聚会时使用。
senses.why: The Latin root tendere means to stretch, so the plainest sense is a thing that can be stretched to a greater length.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 tendere 意为「拉伸」，所以最直接的一层就是能被拉得更长。

senses.title: Able to be stretched out
senses.definition: able to be drawn out or unfolded, as a leg, an arm, or a handle of a device
senses.definitionCN: 能被抽出或展开，如器具的支腿、支臂或把手
senses.example: The tripod has extendable legs that lock at three heights.
senses.exampleCN: 这副三脚架有可伸长的支腿，能在三个高度锁定。
senses.why: A device that stretches outward repeats the same gesture of tendere, adding length piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 器具向外伸出，重复的正是 tendere 那个「一点点拉长」的动作。

senses.title: Able to be widened in scope
senses.definition: able to be enlarged so as to cover more subjects, functions, or territory
senses.definitionCN: 能够扩大以涵盖更多对象、功能或地域
senses.example: The teaching model is extendable to rural schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这套教学模式可以扩展到乡村学校。
senses.why: Once length becomes reach, the word moves easily from tables to plans that cover more ground.
senses.whyCN: 长度一旦变成「触及范围」，这个词就从桌子转到能覆盖更多地方的方案。

senses.title: Able to be postponed
senses.definition: able to be given a later date, as a deadline, a visa, or a period of validity
senses.definitionCN: 能够改到更晚的日期，如截止日期、签证或有效期
senses.example: The submission deadline is extendable by one week on request.
senses.exampleCN: 经申请，提交截止日期可以延后一周。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a line that can be stretched, so a fixed date becomes a date that can be pushed further out.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条可以拉长的线，固定日期于是变成可以往后推的日期。

senses.title: Able to be renewed
senses.definition: able to be continued for a further term, as a lease, a licence, or a contract
senses.definitionCN: 能够再延续一个期限，如租约、执照或合同
senses.example: The lease is extendable for another five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约可以再续五年。
senses.why: A term that can be stretched past its first end follows the same picture as a stretched line.
senses.whyCN: 一个期限能越过原本的终点继续拉长，和拉长一条线是同一幅画面。

senses.title: Able to take more capacity
senses.definition: able to hold more data, power, or storage once extra parts are added
senses.definitionCN: 增加部件后能容纳更多数据、电力或存储
senses.example: The server rack is extendable to twice its present memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机柜可以扩容到现有内存的两倍。
senses.why: Adding modules to a machine is adding length to a frame, so capacity grows by the same outward stretch.
senses.whyCN: 给机器加模块就是给框架加长度，容量靠同样的向外伸展而增长。

senses.title: Able to reach further
senses.definition: able to be carried or laid further outward, as a pipe, a cable, or a route
senses.definitionCN: 能够向外铺设或延伸到更远处，如管道、电缆或路线
senses.example: The water main is extendable to the new housing estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条供水主管可以延伸到新的住宅区。
senses.why: A line that reaches further outward is the most literal picture of stretching in space.
senses.whyCN: 一条线向外伸得更远，是「拉伸」在空间里最字面的画面。

senses.title: Able to be applied more widely
senses.definition: able to be applied to more people or cases, as a rule, a clause, or a definition
senses.definitionCN: 能够适用于更多人或情形，如规则、条款或定义
senses.example: The clause is extendable to subcontractors and their staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款可以扩展到分包商及其员工。
senses.why: A rule stretches over new cases just as a board stretches over a longer table, which is the abstract end of the root.
senses.whyCN: 规则覆盖到新情形，就像木板铺到更长的桌面上，这是词根最抽象的一端。

intro.en: Extendable is the English verb extend plus the suffix -able; extend goes back through French to Latin extendere, to stretch out.
intro.cn: extendable 是英语动词 extend 加词尾 -able；extend 经法语上溯到拉丁语 extendere，意为向外伸展。

items.en: The prefix ex- means out, and tendere means to stretch.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 意为向外，tendere 意为拉伸。

items.en: Extendere joins the two parts and means to stretch out or spread.
items.cn: extendere 把两部分合起来，意为向外伸展、铺开。

items.en: Estendre carries the Latin verb into French.
items.cn: estendre 把这个拉丁语动词带入法语。

items.en: Middle English borrows extend from the French form.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语形式借入 extend。

items.en: Adding -able produces extendable, recorded from the seventeenth century onward.
items.cn: 加上 -able 得到 extendable，文献记录可上溯到十七世纪。

items.en: Modern use spreads from furniture and tools to software and contracts.
items.cn: 现代用法从家具与工具扩展到软件与合同。

note.en: Extendable sits inside the stretch family of extend, extension, and extensible, and beside words such as expandable and stretchable.
note.cn: extendable 属于 extend、extension、extensible 这一「拉伸」词族，也与 expandable、stretchable 这类词相邻。

entries.definition: to make something longer or larger
the act of making something longer or larger
able to be stretched or enlarged
entries.definitionCN: 可伸长的；可扩展的，与 extendable 同根近义

entries.definition: able to be made larger in size or scope
able to be pulled or spread without breaking
able to bend or change without breaking
entries.definitionCN: 可弯曲的；灵活的，强调弯折而非变长

normalIntro.en: Extendable is simply extend plus -able: anything that can be stretched further can carry this label.
normalIntro.cn: extendable 就是 extend 加 -able：凡是能被拉得更长的东西，都可以用这个词。

normal.en: Extend plus -able gives extendable, so the word means able to be extended.
normal.cn: extend 加 -able 构成 extendable，意思就是「能被延长的」。

normal.en: An extendable table keeps an extra leaf hidden under its top.
normal.cn: 可加长的餐桌在桌面底下藏着一块备用活动板。

normal.en: Extendable legs let a tripod stand steady on uneven ground.
normal.cn: 可伸长的支腿让三脚架在不平的地面上也站得稳。

normal.en: A deadline called extendable can be moved to a later date.
normal.cn: 被称作 extendable 的截止日期，可以改到更晚的一天。

normal.en: Compare extendable with flexible: flexible bends, while extendable grows longer.
normal.cn: 对比 flexible：flexible 强调弯曲，extendable 强调变长。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden leaf sliding out from under a table top.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板从桌面底下滑出来，桌子随之变长。

abstract.en: Imagine a tripod leg clicking out one metal ring at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象三脚架的支腿一节节咔哒抽出，一节比一节长。

abstract.en: Think of a map that unfolds to show one more district at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图展开后，边缘又多出一个街区。

examples.en: The firm bought an extendable table so that the meeting room could seat twelve.
examples.cn: 公司买了一张可加长的餐桌，好让会议室能坐十二个人。

examples.en: The crane carries an extendable arm that can reach the top of the tower.
examples.cn: 这台吊车带有可伸缩的支臂，能够够到塔顶。

examples.en: The visa is extendable once, provided the student keeps a full course load.
examples.cn: 只要学生保持满课程负担，这张签证可以延期一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊克斯腾德波」——谐音近似「一拉，桌就腾出空位」：桌子一拉就变长，所以是「可延长的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ tendere（拉伸）→ extendere（向外伸展）→ 古法语 estendre → 英语 extend；再加形容词词尾 -able 得 extendable，核心义是「能向外拉长」。

sensesIntro.en: Extendable starts from a board pulled out to lengthen a table, then covers parts that stretch out, plans that reach wider, dates pushed later, and rules that stretch to new cases.
sensesIntro.cn: extendable 从一块拉出来加长桌面的木板出发，继而涵盖能抽出的部件、覆盖更广的方案、往后推的日期，以及延伸到新情形的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hidden board pulled out, so the table grows longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块藏着的木板被拉出来，桌子随之变长。

branches.en: A leaf pulled from a table is the physical sense of added length.
branches.cn: 从桌面抽出的活动板，是「增加长度」这一物理义项。

branches.en: A leg or an arm drawn outward is the device sense.
branches.cn: 向外抽出的支腿或支臂，是器具层面的义项。

branches.en: A plan that covers more subjects is the scope sense.
branches.cn: 覆盖更多对象的方案，是范围层面的义项。

branches.en: A deadline or a lease pushed later treats time as a line that stretches.
branches.cn: 截止日期或租约往后推，把时间当成一条可拉长的线。

branches.en: Memory, pipes, and rules all grow by adding length outward.
branches.cn: 内存、管道与规则都靠向外加长而增长。

intro.en: Extendable joins the Latin prefix ex- and the root tendere, then takes the English suffix -able; extend, extension, and extensible belong to the same family.
intro.cn: extendable 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与词根 tendere 构成，再加英语词尾 -able；extend、extension 与 extensible 都属于同一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere means to stretch, and extendere means to stretch out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为拉伸，extendere 意为向外伸展。

items.example: The prefix ex- carries the idea of outward motion.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 带来向外运动的意味。

items.example: Tendere is the root of tension and of extend.
items.exampleCN: tendere 是 tension 与 extend 共同的词根。

items.example: Extendere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: extendere 把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.example: You extend a table by adding a leaf.
items.exampleCN: 给餐桌加一块活动板，就是把桌子延长。

items.example: The suffix -able turns verbs into adjectives of possibility.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 把动词变成表示「能够」的形容词。

items.example: Extendable describes what can be stretched further.
items.exampleCN: extendable 描述能被拉得更长的事物。

items.example: Extension names the act that extendable makes possible.
items.exampleCN: extension 指 extendable 所允许的那种延长行为。

items.example: Extensible is the Latin-flavoured twin of extendable.
items.exampleCN: extensible 是 extendable 带拉丁味的同义兄弟。

items.example: Distend keeps tendere but changes the prefix.
items.exampleCN: distend 保留 tendere，只换了前缀。

items.example: Tension is what a stretched thing feels.
items.exampleCN: tension 就是被拉紧的东西所承受的力。

definition_en: the act of making something longer or larger; an added part of a building; extra time; a phone line connected to one system

scene: 我们申请延长截止日期。We asked for an extension of the deadline.

senses.title: The act of extending

senses.definitionCN: 使某物更长或更大的行为
senses.example: The extension of the railway took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路的延伸用了两年。
senses.why: The core sense is the act of stretching out.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是向外伸展的行为。

senses.title: An added part

senses.definitionCN: 加建在建筑物上的额外部分

senses.exampleCN: 他们在后面建了一个小扩建部分。

senses.title: Extra time

senses.example: The teacher gave us an extension.
senses.exampleCN: 老师给了我们延期。

senses.title: Phone line

senses.definitionCN: 连接到主线上的电话分线

senses.why: A branch line extends from the main one.

intro.en: Extension comes from Latin extensio, from extendere, to stretch out.

normal.en: The library needs an extension at the back.

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands move more slowly.

abstract.en: Think of one main road splitting into a side lane.

examples.en: The council approved the extension of the school.
examples.cn: 议会批准了学校的扩建。

examples.cn: 他获得了两周的延期。

examples.en: Her office extension is not working.

senses.definitionCN: 覆盖大片区域或很大范围的

senses.title: Very great in amount

definition_zh: 消灭；灭绝；根除；屠杀整个族群
definition_en: to kill or destroy a whole group of living things so that none are left, or to get rid of something harmful completely
core_image: 一整群害虫被药雾扫过，最后一只也翻倒在墙角
scene: 老房子翻修时，工人发现墙缝里爬满白蚁，决定一次性清干净。When the old house was renovated, the workers decided to exterminate the termites living in its walls.
sceneCN: 这里 exterminate 是「消灭；灭杀」（第 1 个义项：用药物或陷阱把一整群害虫杀死）；句意：老房子翻修时，工人决定消灭墙里的白蚁。

pos.zh: 消灭；灭绝；根除；屠杀整个族群

derivatives.zh: 由 exterminate 加名词词尾 -ion 构成，义为「灭绝；彻底消灭」
由 exterminate 加施事词尾 -or 构成，义为「灭害人员；除虫工」
由 exterminate 加 -able 构成，义为「可被消灭的」，使用较少

senses.title: To kill pests in large numbers
senses.definition: to kill a whole group of insects, rats, or other pests, usually with chemicals or traps
senses.definitionCN: 用药物或陷阱把一整群昆虫、老鼠等害虫杀死
senses.example: The council hired a team to exterminate the rats in the food market.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门雇了一队人来消灭食品市场里的老鼠。
senses.why: Latin ex- means out and terminus means boundary, so exterminare first meant to drive a group out beyond the boundary and later to kill it off entirely.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ex- 意为「出、外」，terminus 意为「边界」，exterminare 本指把一群东西赶出边界之外，后来转为「整群杀灭」；害虫正是最常被整群赶尽杀绝的对象。

senses.title: To wipe out a species
senses.definition: to destroy a species or a kind of living thing so that none of it is left anywhere
senses.definitionCN: 把某个物种或某一类生物彻底毁掉，使其在任何地方都不再留存
senses.example: Hunters and shrinking habitat have exterminated several island species.
senses.exampleCN: 捕猎与栖息地缩小已经使好几个岛屿物种灭绝。
senses.why: Once the boundary moved from land to life itself, driving a kind past the edge of existence became the sense of making a species disappear.
senses.whyCN: 当「边界」从土地移到生命本身，把一类生物赶出存在的边缘，就成了「使物种消失」这一义项。

senses.title: To kill a whole people
senses.definition: to kill a whole population or people, especially in a deliberate and violent way
senses.definitionCN: 蓄意以暴力杀死整个族群或全部人口
senses.example: The invading army tried to exterminate the villagers in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵军队试图屠杀山谷里的村民。
senses.why: The same total logic, now applied to human groups, gives the word its gravest sense of wiping out a people.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「整群清除」逻辑一旦用到人身上，就产生了这个词最沉重的义项：把一整个族群杀绝。

senses.title: To destroy something utterly
senses.definition: to destroy a place or a thing so completely that nothing of it remains, used chiefly in literary or historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 把某个地方或某样东西彻底毁掉，什么都不剩，主要用于书面或历史叙述
senses.example: A long siege had exterminated every house outside the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 长期围城把城墙外的房屋全部摧毁。
senses.why: Because the verb already means total removal, older writers could use it for places and objects as well as living things.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个动词本身就带「彻底清除」的意思，较早的写作者便把它用到地方与器物上，而不限于生物。

senses.title: To root out a harmful practice
senses.definition: to get rid of a harmful practice, condition, or trade completely, used in formal and figurative writing
senses.definitionCN: 彻底清除某种有害的做法、状况或交易，用于正式或比喻性的文字
senses.example: The new agency was set up to exterminate corruption in the customs service.
senses.exampleCN: 新设的机构是为了根除海关的腐败。
senses.why: The word carries the force of total removal, so public writers borrow it for evils that must be cleared out root and branch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带有「连根清除」的力量，写作者便借它来形容必须彻底铲除的恶弊。

intro.en: Exterminate comes from Latin ex-, out of, and terminus, a boundary stone, through the verb exterminare, to drive beyond the boundary.
intro.cn: exterminate 来自拉丁语 ex-（出、外）与 terminus（界石、边界），经由动词 exterminare（赶出边界之外）进入英语。

items.en: Terminus is a boundary stone, the marker that fixes where a piece of land ends.
items.cn: terminus 是界石，是标出土地尽头的标记。

items.en: Exterminare means to drive a person or a thing out beyond those boundaries.
items.cn: exterminare 意为把人或物赶出那些边界之外。

items.en: Late Latin widens the verb to mean to destroy or remove something entirely.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把这个动词扩展为「彻底摧毁、清除」。

items.en: Old French exterminer carries the stronger sense of total removal.
items.cn: 古法语 exterminer 带着「彻底清除」的更强含义。

items.en: English first uses exterminate for banishing a group and later for destroying it completely.
items.cn: 英语最初用 exterminate 表示把一群人驱逐出去，后来才表示彻底消灭。

items.en: Modern English applies the verb mainly to pests, species, and peoples.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词主要用在害虫、物种与族群上。

note.en: Exterminate belongs to the terminus family of boundary words and sits close to verbs for total destruction.
note.cn: exterminate 属于 terminus 这一「边界」词族，同时也靠近一批表示「彻底摧毁」的动词。

normalIntro.en: Exterminate is a boundary word: ex-, out, plus terminus, the stone that marks the end of a field.

normal.en: Pest controllers exterminate rats and cockroaches for a living.

normal.en: A species is exterminated when not one breeding pair is left.

normal.en: Historians use exterminate for the deliberate killing of a whole people.
normal.cn: 历史学家用 exterminate 指对整个族群的蓄意屠杀。

normal.cn: 对比 eliminate：eliminate 中性，exterminate 强调整体消灭，且常带暴力色彩。

examples.en: Hunting and the loss of habitat have exterminated several island species.

examples.en: The new ministry was created to exterminate corruption in the customs service.

sensesIntro.en: Exterminate begins with the image of driving a group past the boundary, then hardens into killing off pests, wiping out a species, destroying a people, and, by extension, rooting out a harmful practice.
sensesIntro.cn: exterminate 起于「把一群东西赶出边界」的画面，随后固化为整群杀灭害虫、使物种灭绝、屠杀族群，并引申为根除有害的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole colony driven past the boundary stone until nothing is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整群生物被赶过界石，直到什么都不剩。

branches.en: Killing a whole infestation is the everyday sense of the verb.
branches.cn: 把一整群害虫杀灭，是这个动词最日常的义项。

branches.en: Pushing a kind past the edge of existence gives the sense of extinction.
branches.cn: 把一类生物推过存在的边缘，就有了「灭绝」这一义项。

branches.en: The same total removal, aimed at people, is the gravest sense.
branches.cn: 同样的「整群清除」用到人身上，就是最沉重的义项。

branches.en: Total removal of a place or thing is the older, literary extension.
branches.cn: 把地方或器物彻底清除，是较早的书面引申。

branches.en: Pests and harmful practices are both cleared out root and branch.
branches.cn: 害虫与有害做法都是被连根清除的对象。

intro.en: Exterminate joins the Latin prefix ex- and the noun terminus, a boundary, and English has built a small family of nouns and agent words around the verb.
intro.cn: exterminate 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与名词 terminus（边界）结合而成，英语围绕这个动词又造出若干名词与施事词。
